CheckTitle: CloudWatch Log Groups have a data protection policy configured
CheckType: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Description: **CloudWatch log groups** are checked to ensure a **data protection policy** is configured to audit and mask sensitive data identifiers such as PII and credentials.
Risk: Without a data protection policy, sensitive data written to CloudWatch Logs is stored in clear text and accessible to every principal with logs:GetLogEvents permission, widening exposure of regulated or confidential information.

Code.NativeIaC:
```yaml
# CloudFormation: Configure a Data Protection Policy on a CloudWatch Log Group
Resources:
  <example_resource_name>:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: <example_resource_name>
      DataProtectionPolicy:
        Name: data-protection-policy
        Version: "2021-06-01"
        Statement:
          - Sid: audit
            DataIdentifier:
              - arn:aws:dataprotection::aws:data-identifier/EmailAddress
            Operation:
              Audit:
                FindingsDestination: {}
          - Sid: redact
            DataIdentifier:
              - arn:aws:dataprotection::aws:data-identifier/EmailAddress
            Operation:
              Deidentify:
                MaskConfig: {}
```
Code.Other:
1. In the AWS Console, open CloudWatch > Logs > Log groups
2. Select the log group
3. Choose Actions > Create data protection policy
4. Under Managed data identifiers, select the data types to protect (e.g. EmailAddress, CreditCardNumber)
5. (Optional) Choose a destination for the audit findings report
6. Choose Activate data protection

Recommendation.Text: Attach a data protection policy to CloudWatch Log Groups that may contain sensitive data. Choose managed data identifiers matching the data types your applications can log, or create an account-level policy to cover all log groups.

Notes: This check evaluates all CloudWatch Log Groups in scope. It retrieves the detailed data protection policy document via GetDataProtectionPolicy to confirm that an active policy exists.
